OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 (2024)
cleanIntro: SIG's own field strip for the SIG MPX, in SIG's order and no further. The MPX is a gas operated 9mm firing from a rotating locking closed bolt, so unlike a blowback pistol-calibre carbine it has a bolt with lugs, a cam pin and a short-stroke op rod that all carry carbon. This book covers the MPX, the MPX-K and the MPX PCC together, and it is written for both SAFE-SEMI and SAFE-SEMI-AUTO variants — where a step belongs to only one of those, the manual's own qualifier is carried through. Handguard, barrel and gas piston removal are published past the field strip and are kept in the deep clean.

steps.title: Magazine out of the receiver first
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction, keep your finger off the trigger, and press the ambidextrous magazine catch while pulling the magazine down out of the lower receiver. Set it aside off the bench.
steps.prose: The MPX magazine does not always drop free the way an AR magazine does — the double-stack 9mm body is a friction fit in the well when it is dirty, so SIG tells you to press and pull at the same time rather than press and wait. Getting the magazine out is only the first half of clearing; the chamber is a separate question you have not asked yet.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine from the firearm by pressing the magazine catch and simultaneously pulling the magazine from the receiver.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 3.3 Unloading and Clearing the SIG MPX, step 2, p.38
steps.warn: An MPX with the magazine out will still fire a chambered round. There is no magazine disconnect on this firearm.

steps.title: Bottom of the bolt catch, then charge briskly
steps.action: Press and hold the BOTTOM portion of the bolt catch with your support hand, then pull the charging handle briskly and fully to the rear with the other. The carrier should stop and stay back against the catch. Return the charging handle forward until it locks, and rotate the fire control selector to SAFE.
steps.prose: The MPX bolt catch is one lever with two jobs: the bottom half locks the carrier back and the top half releases it. Press the top half by mistake and the carrier runs forward under full spring load with your hand still on the charging handle. Briskly matters too — ease the handle back slowly and the catch will not have time to rise into the carrier notch, and the bolt will simply follow your hand forward again.
steps.quote: Press and hold the bottom portion of the bolt catch while pulling the charging handle briskly and fully to the rear. The bolt carrier assembly should remain locked to the rear.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 3.3 Unloading and Clearing the SIG MPX, step 3, p.39

steps.title: Inspect chamber, bolt face and magazine well
steps.action: With the carrier held back, look into the ejection port at the chamber and the bolt face, then look up into the empty magazine well. Do it by eye and confirm with a finger — a 9mm case rim in a dark receiver reads as shadow.
steps.prose: Two things hide on an MPX: a live round that failed to eject and sits nose-down in the well, and a spent case standing on the bolt face behind the extractor. Neither is visible from above the receiver; both are obvious from the port with the muzzle down and light behind you.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber, bolt face, and magazine well to ensure that there are no live rounds or spent cartridges present.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 3.3 Unloading and Clearing the SIG MPX, step 4, p.40
steps.warn: Keep every finger clear of the bolt catch while you inspect. The carriage assembly is under spring tension and closes forcefully the moment the catch is pressed.

steps.title: Selector on SAFE, sling off
steps.action: With the firearm cleared, confirm the fire control selector is rotated fully to SAFE and visually check that it is — partway is not on SAFE. Then unclip any sling, because a loose sling swivel on the handguard will drag the upper around as you swing the receivers open.
steps.prose: SIG restates the clear at the head of the field strip rather than assuming you did it a page ago, and that is deliberate: the next move separates the receivers with the hammer still cocked under the carrier. A selector left between positions leaves the trigger live for that whole sequence.
steps.quote: Unload and clear the firearm. Ensure the fire control selector is on SAFE.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 1, p.50

steps.title: Takedown pin left to right, to the detent
steps.action: Push the rear takedown pin from the left side of the lower receiver towards the right. It travels a short distance and then stops hard against its detent — that stop is the end of the movement, not an obstruction.
steps.prose: The pin is captive and is not meant to come out of the receiver. Owners coming off an AR-15 expect a pin that pulls clear and keep pushing or start prying, which bends the detent and leaves a pin that will not stay put. If it will not start moving, the receivers are still under load from the recoil spring; press the upper and lower together and push again.
steps.quote: Push takedown pin from left to right until stopped by detent.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 3, p.50

steps.title: Swing the receivers open on the pivot pin
steps.action: With the takedown pin at its detent, hinge the upper receiver up and away from the lower, pivoting on the front pin. The two halves should open smoothly to roughly the angle of an opened AR.
steps.prose: Nothing is loose yet — the carriage assembly is still in the upper and the hammer is still cocked in the lower. Support the upper as it opens rather than letting it hang on the pivot pin, because the handguard and barrel out front give it enough leverage to spring the pin's detent.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 4, p.51

steps.title: Retract the charging handle until it stops
steps.action: With the receivers open, draw the non-reciprocating charging handle rearward until it reaches its stop and hold it there.
steps.prose: This is what unlocks the carriage from the handle's latches and lines the carrier up with the opening at the rear of the upper. Let the handle run back forward now and the carriage re-engages, and the next step will feel jammed rather than merely stiff.
steps.quote: Retract charging handle until it stops.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 5, p.52

steps.title: Draw the carriage assembly out by the recoil spring plate
steps.action: Grasp the recoil spring plate at the rear of the carrier and pull the whole carriage assembly straight back and out of the upper receiver. Carrier, bolt, op rod, recoil springs and plate all come away together.
steps.prose: The MPX's recoil springs live inside the upper receiver behind the carrier rather than in a buffer tube, which is why this gun folds its stock and why the plate is the only safe handle. Pull on the springs or the guide rods instead and you unseat the assembly inside the receiver, and it binds crosswise on the way out.
steps.quote: Grasp recoil spring plate and pull carriage assembly from upper receiver. It will come out as a complete unit.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 6, p.53

steps.title: Charging handle out of the receiver
steps.action: With the carriage gone, slide the charging handle rearward and lift it out of its channel in the upper receiver.
steps.prose: It only leaves once the carriage is out, because the carriage is what holds the handle's tabs in their track. Note which way the latch tabs face as it comes away — the handle goes back in by lining those tabs up with a cutout, and there is only one orientation that works.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 7, p.54

steps.title: Close the receivers, push the pivot pin, separate
steps.action: Bring the upper and lower back together, push the front pivot pin from left to right until it reaches its detent, then lift the two receivers apart.
steps.prose: The receivers have to be closed for this — the pivot pin passes through both halves and through the handguard link out front, and none of those holes line up with the gun hinged open. Closing first is also what keeps the pin square in its bore, so it does not gall the aluminium as it moves.
steps.quote: Close receivers together and push pivot pin from left to right, then separate receivers.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 8, p.55

steps.title: Recoil assembly up, then out to the left
steps.action: Take the carriage assembly and rotate the recoil assembly upward away from the bolt carrier, then slide it out from the LEFT side of the carrier.
steps.prose: Up first, then left — the rotation is what lifts the op rod lug clear of its pocket in the carrier before anything slides. Try to pull it straight off to the rear and the lug stays hooked, and the force ends up on the op rod rather than on the joint you meant to open.
steps.quote: Rotate recoil assembly upward and slide it out from left side of bolt carrier.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 9, p.56

steps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out
steps.action: Push the firing pin retaining pin out of the right side of the bolt carrier and set it somewhere it cannot roll. It is a small split pin, not a solid one.
steps.prose: On reassembly SIG puts it back from the right side with the split oriented vertically and behind the large flange of the firing pin, so take a moment to see how it sits now. Lose this pin and the firing pin walks out the back of the carrier under recoil, which ends the range trip.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 10, p.57

steps.title: Firing pin and spring out the rear of the carrier
steps.action: Tip the carrier nose-down and let the firing pin and its spring come out of the rear. They should slide out under their own weight with no persuasion.
steps.prose: If the firing pin will not move, the retaining pin is still in — nothing here is a press fit. The spring stays captive on the pin; keep them together as a pair so the spring does not end up on the wrong end at reassembly.
steps.quote: Remove firing pin and spring from rear of bolt carrier.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 11, p.58

steps.title: Cam pin out, then the bolt forward out of the carrier
steps.action: Push the bolt slightly rearward in the carrier to free the cam pin, rotate the cam pin a quarter turn and lift it straight out, then draw the bolt out of the FRONT of the carrier.
steps.prose: The cam pin is what makes the bolt rotate and lock into the barrel extension, and it can only be lifted when its slot lines up with the clearance cut in the carrier. Forward is the only exit for the bolt; it will not come out backwards past the carrier's firing pin bore.
steps.quote: Remove cam pin from bolt, then remove bolt from front of carrier.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 12, p.59
steps.warn: Put the cam pin somewhere you cannot leave it behind. SIG's own warning is that failure to install the cam pin may result in serious injury or death to the user and catastrophic damage to the firearm.

steps.title: Extractor off the bolt — and what to leave alone
steps.action: Push the extractor pin out to the right side of the bolt and lift the extractor out of its slot. Stop there: leave the O-ring on the extractor, and leave the extractor spring and insert in the bolt.
steps.prose: That O-ring is a booster that adds tension to the extractor spring, and SIG only wants it out below -20°F or when it is being replaced. Pulling it out for a routine clean and stretching it back on is how an MPX develops failures to extract two range trips later. The extractor pin comes out to the right and goes back in from the right, so keep it on the right of the bench.
steps.quote: Push extractor pin out to right side and remove extractor from the bolt. Do not remove O-ring unless operating in temperatures below -20°F or replacement is necessary.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.1 Field Strip the SIG MPX, step 13, p.60

steps.title: Carbon on the operating parts is scraped, not brushed
steps.action: Work the solvent over the bolt body, the bolt lugs, the cam pin, the op rod and the bolt channel of the carrier, then attack the hard glazed carbon with a scraper or a brass pick rather than a brush.
steps.prose: The MPX taps propellant gas at the block and drives a short-stroke piston, so every surface downstream of that tap carries baked carbon rather than soft fouling. A nylon brush polishes it and moves nothing. Watch the op rod lug that engages the carrier and the back of the bolt lugs — that is where build-up starts short-stroking the gun.
steps.caution: No wire brushes on the upper or lower receiver — they are aluminium and a wire brush scratches the finish straight off.
steps.quote: Wherever propellant gases directly contact operating system parts, carbon will build up. Carbon cannot be removed with a brush and must be scraped.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 5.0 Cleaning and Lubrication, p.66

steps.title: Lubricate the lower — and read the auto sear qualifier
steps.action: Put one to two drops of lubricant where the hammer, the trigger and the bolt catch bear on their pins, one to two drops on the selector where it contacts the lower receiver, and one to two drops on the pivot and takedown pins. On a semi-automatic MPX that is three parts on this line, not four.
steps.prose: SIG prints this line for every MPX, but it names a part that a semi-automatic gun does not have: the AUTO SEAR, qualified in the manual's own words as auto variants only. The MPX is sold in SAFE-SEMI and SAFE-SEMI-AUTO variants, and only the select-fire version carries a sear to oil. If your lower has no AUTO position on the selector, do not go hunting for a fourth pin behind the hammer — there is nothing there, and probing for it only pushes lubricant into the trigger group where it collects grit.
steps.aside: The same qualifier turns up again in the function check: SIG's step 9 is "Rotate the selector to AUTO (if applicable)", and steps 9 through 15 exist only for the select-fire gun.
steps.quote: Apply 1 to 2 drops of lubricant to the hammer, trigger, auto sear (auto variants only), and bolt catch where theses parts contact their respective pins.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 5.4 Lubrication — Lower Receiver, item A, p.75

steps.title: Bolt face and gas plug stay dry
steps.action: Oil the bolt carrier contact surfaces, the back of the bolt lugs, the cam pin and the spring guide rods — then deliberately wipe the face of the bolt and the gas plug back to dry.
steps.prose: Those two surfaces sit directly in the gas and primer blast. Lubricant there does not stay lubricant; it cooks into a varnish that glues carbon to the bolt face and can seize the gas plug in the block, which is the part you need to rotate to service the piston. Everywhere else on this gun, thin films and single drops — over-oiling an MPX collects the very carbon you just scraped off.
steps.quote: Do not lubricate the face of the bolt or the gas plug.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 5.4 Lubrication — Carriage Assembly, item F, p.72

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the lower receiver, the upper receiver with barrel and handguard still on it, the charging handle, and the carriage assembly broken down into carrier, bolt, cam pin, firing pin and spring, retaining pin, extractor and pin, and the recoil assembly. That is the whole of SIG's user level for the MPX.
steps.prose: The handguard, barrel and gas piston can still come off for a deep clean, and those are published in this manual as sections 4.2 through 4.4. Anything past that — the fire control group out of the lower, the gas block off the barrel, the extractor insert out of the bolt — is armorer work in SIG's own words and voids the warranty.
steps.quote: Do not attempt to disassemble your SIG SAUER firearm beyond the point explained in this manual.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 1.0 Safety Warnings — Replacement Parts, p.5

deepSteps.title: Pivot pin to its detent, handguard forward off the upper
deepSteps.action: With the carriage assembly already out, push the front pivot pin out to its detent and pull the handguard straight forward off the upper receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The MPX handguard is not clamped to a barrel nut — it is retained by the pivot pin passing through a link at its rear, which is why the same pin does two jobs. Pull the handguard before the pin is at its detent and you will be levering the link against a steel pin; it feels like the handguard is glued on, and it is not.
deepSteps.quote: The handguard is held on by the pivot pin passing through the handguard link as shown. To remove, pull pivot pin out to detent, then pull handguard forward off of upper receiver.
deepSteps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.2 Handguard Removal, p.61

deepSteps.title: Two barrel clamping screws, T25, right side
deepSteps.action: Confirm the carriage assembly is already out, then use a T25 drive bit to back out both barrel clamping screws from the RIGHT side of the upper receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The carriage has to be gone first because the bolt lugs engage the barrel extension whenever the carrier is forward — with it in place the barrel is mechanically locked to the receiver and no amount of loosening will free it. Use a proper T25 bit, not a near-fit hex key; these screws are torqued and the sockets round off cheaply.
deepSteps.quote: Use a T25 drive bit to loosen and remove the two barrel clamping screws from the right side of the upper receiver.
deepSteps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.3 Barrel Removal, step 1, p.62

deepSteps.title: Barrel clamp off the left side
deepSteps.action: Lift the barrel clamp out of the left side of the receiver. If carbon has stuck it in place, thread one of the screws you just removed into it from the left side and use that as a handle to draw it gently out.
deepSteps.prose: SIG gives you the screw trick precisely because the clamp sits in a blind pocket with nothing to grip — prying it with a screwdriver marks the receiver and can deform the clamp, and a deformed clamp will not hold barrel index the next time you torque it down.
deepSteps.quote: Remove barrel clamp from left side of receiver. If the barrel clamp is stuck, thread one of the screws in from the left side and gently pull it out.
deepSteps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.3 Barrel Removal, step 2, p.63

deepSteps.title: Barrel straight out of the upper
deepSteps.action: Draw the barrel forward out of the upper receiver in one straight pull, keeping it in line with the receiver bore the whole way.
deepSteps.prose: The instinct when a barrel feels tight is to rock it side to side, and on an aluminium-receivered MPX that is the one thing that does real damage — the barrel extension bears on the receiver's inner surfaces and wiggling gouges them. If it is tight, check that both clamping screws are fully out and that the clamp itself has left.
deepSteps.caution: Do not wiggle the barrel back and forth to remove it — SIG's own caution is that this can damage the upper receiver.
deepSteps.quote: Pull barrel straight out of upper receiver.
deepSteps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.3 Barrel Removal, step 3, p.64

deepSteps.title: Gas plug a half turn, then plug and piston out the front
deepSteps.action: Rotate the gas plug 180 degrees until the flange on the plug is fully exposed, then pull the plug and the piston out of the front of the gas block.
deepSteps.prose: The flange is the tell — half a turn and it clears its cut in the block, and until you can see the whole flange the plug is still captured. Forcing it before then twists on a carbon-seized part. This is also why the plug is on the do-not-lubricate list: oil in the block bakes and seizes exactly this rotation.
deepSteps.quote: Rotate gas plug 180 degrees until flange on plug is fully exposed, allowing plug to be pulled out of gas block.
deepSteps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 4.4 Gas Plug and Piston Removal, step 1, p.65

deepSteps.title: Scrape the firing pin channel in the bolt
deepSteps.action: Insert the scraper tool into the firing pin slot in the rear of the bolt assembly and spin it to cut the carbon ring out of the channel.
deepSteps.prose: That channel is a blind hole directly behind the primer, so it fills with hard carbon that a patch cannot reach and a brush cannot cut. Left alone it packs solid, the firing pin loses its free travel, and the gun starts producing light strikes that read like an ammunition problem.
deepSteps.quote: The scraper tool is used to remove carbon buildup for the firing pin channel of the bolt assembly.
deepSteps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 5.3 Scraper Tool, p.70

deepSteps.title: Carbon off the piston and plug
deepSteps.action: With the piston and plug out of the gas block, scrape the carbon shell off both, paying attention to the piston's outside diameter and the plug's flange faces.
deepSteps.prose: Piston-driven guns run dirtiest right here, and a piston with a carbon collar on it drags in the block and delivers a short, weak stroke to the op rod. The symptom is a bolt that fails to lock back on an empty magazine — people chase the magazine and the springs when the answer is a five-minute scrape.
deepSteps.quote: Remove carbon buildup from piston and plug.
deepSteps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 5.2 Cleaning the Operating System, item M, p.68

deepSteps.title: If you shoot it suppressed, do all of this more often
deepSteps.action: Take the suppressor off before you touch the bore, then increase how often you run this whole deep clean rather than doing anything different when you get there.
deepSteps.prose: A can raises back pressure in a gas gun, and on the MPX that pushes more residue back through the piston, along the op rod and into the receiver. SIG's answer is frequency, not technique. And never run patches down the bore with the suppressor still fitted — a patch that separates inside the can is a bore obstruction you cannot see.
deepSteps.caution: Do not run patches through the bore with a sound suppressor attached.
deepSteps.quote: If the MPX is used with a suppressor attached, the back pressure will produce more residue, which will require attention. It is suggested to increase the frequency of regular maintenance.
deepSteps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
SIG MPX 
® — P/N 1811295-01 REV07 — 5.2 Cleaning the Operating System, p.68

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Suppressor OFF before any patch goes down the bore
Jag of the right calibre on the rod; CLP-wet patch pushed toward the muzzle
Let the CLP stand several minutes to loosen fouling, then a fresh wet patch
Bore brush only if fouling is heavy, then a wet patch to carry off what it lifted
Dry patches until they come out clean
Chamber brush wet with CLP, muzzle kept elevated so CLP does not run back into the clean bore
Plunging strokes plus full 360 degree rotations in the barrel extension to clear the locking lug area

cleaning.name: OPERATING SYSTEM
tasks: Bolt body in solvent; carbon off the bolt lugs and out of the hood of the extractor
Recoil spring rods and recoil springs cleaned down
Op rod cleaned, with attention to residue on the lug that engages the bolt carrier
Cam pin and the op rod interface of the carrier scraped clear of carbon
Firing pin, spring and carrier body wiped down; bolt channel cleared of build-up
Firing pin retaining pin and extractor pin cleaned
Carbon removed from piston and plug

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION — CARRIAGE ASSEMBLY
tasks: 1 to 2 drops where the op rod contacts the spring guide, recoil plate and bolt carrier
Thin film on the spring guide rods and recoil springs
Thin coat on the back of the bolt lugs, the bolt body and the cam pin hole
Thin coat on the bolt carrier contact surfaces; 1 to 2 drops on the cam pin
Bolt face and gas plug: nothing at all

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION — UPPER RECEIVER
tasks: Thin film inside the upper where the carriage assembly rides
Thin film on the sides of the charging handle
1 to 2 drops on the charging handle latches

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION — LOWER RECEIVER
tasks: 1 to 2 drops on hammer, trigger and bolt catch where they bear on their pins
AUTO SEAR: auto variants only — a SAFE-SEMI MPX has no sear on this line
1 to 2 drops on the selector where it contacts the lower receiver
1 to 2 drops on the pivot and takedown pins

reassembly: Piston and gas plug back into the gas block, then rotate the plug 180 degrees to lock it.

Barrel: clean mating surfaces, check the index pins for damage or looseness, slide the barrel in with the index pin engaged in its slot, fit the barrel clamp, start both T25 screws several turns each, then tighten alternately until the clamp is firmly seated and torque both to 30 in-lbf.
Handguard slides on with the handguard link lined up with the hole in the upper receiver.

Bolt: extractor on with its pin in from the RIGHT side; bolt into the carrier with the extractor oriented as SIG shows; cam pin in and aligned so the firing pin bore is clear; firing pin and spring into the rear.

Push the firing pin fully in, install the firing pin retaining pin from the right side with the split vertical, release the firing pin, then confirm the retaining pin sits BEHIND the large flange of the firing pin.
Recoil assembly into the carrier from the left side. Do NOT install the extractor O-ring if operating at or below -20°F.
Upper to lower on the pivot pin with the handguard fully rearward and the pin through the cutout in the handguard link.
Charging handle in halfway, lining its tabs up with the cutout in the upper; carriage assembly in; then push the charging handle forward until it locks.
Press and hold the spring plate until it is inside the upper receiver, close the receivers together, and push the takedown pin back into place.
fncheck: Unloaded, cleared, on SAFE with the bolt forward and locked. Insert an empty magazine and pull down to check it is seated. Pull the charging handle fully back — the bolt must lock back on the empty magazine; push the handle forward until it locks. Press the magazine release: the magazine must fall free under its own weight. Pull the charging handle fully back — a slight click, and the bolt catch visibly rotates upward — then release. Press and hold the bottom of the bolt catch, pull the charging handle fully back so the bolt locks, return the handle forward and press the bolt release on the right side of the upper; the bolt should run forward and lock. On SAFE, press the trigger: nothing happens. On SEMI (FIRE), press and hold: the hammer falls. Holding the trigger back, pull the charging handle fully to the rear and release, then slowly release the trigger — an audible click and a felt sear reset. Steps 9 through 16 of SIG's check, which run the selector to AUTO, apply only if your MPX has an AUTO position.
